analysis: The only change is documentation in docs/developer/test.md (head lines ~142-153): the CI build-cache description now says only pushes to dev/master save a cache and PRs restore the base entry and save nothing. It also adds a note that the MiMo audio gate (testNativeAudioRelease, 1.87 GB codec fixture) runs only when its inputs change or on master pushes. The supplied units are unchanged surrounding base text (lines 457-1385) covering test procedures for the prefix-cache SSD tier, add-on hold, App Attest dispatch, endpoint resumption and logout, native serving qualification and cluster checks. No source, protocol, key-handling, authorization or runtime behavior changes. Relevant threat IDs (T-041, T-053, T-059, T-060, TB-011, TB-012) are described by tests only and no control is altered. Two items are outside the supplied evidence: the actual CI workflow and scripts (scripts/ci-component-paths.py, the cache save conditions in .github/workflows) and whether the doc matches them. Restricting cache saves to trusted branches is, if anything, a cache-poisoning hardening, but it is not verifiable here. Skipping the audio gate on unrelated PRs could in principle reduce PR-time coverage, but the docs say master pushes run every component, so no concrete security regression is established. No findings.
